newsitem.title: SRI LANKA: INTERVIEW-DFCC eyes Comm Bank stake.
newsitem.headline: INTERVIEW-DFCC eyes Comm Bank stake.

text.p: DFCC Bank said on Wednesday it was continuing to discuss with Standard Chartered Plc the possibility of taking a stake in Sri Lanka's Comercial Bank.
DFCC Bank chief executive Moksevi Prelis told Reuters he believed a tie-up with Commercial Bank could produce useful synergies and help DFCC offer a better service to its clients.
"We have got the permission of the Central Bank for taking a major portion of Commercial Bank. We may form a strategic alliance with Commercial Bank in future," he said in an interview.
But he said negotiations were not completed.

Commercial Bank said in April that Standard Chartered had been given permission by Sri Lanka's Central Bank to sell its 40 percent stake, or 10 million shares, in Commercial Bank under certain strict conditions.
The sale could be to DFCC and Hatton National Bank, with DFCC taking 6.25 million shares and Hatton 2.5 million.
The balance shares would have to go to existing Commercial Bank shareholders other than DFCC or Hatton.
The Central Bank also stipulated that DFCC should not end up with more than 25 percent of the voting shares in Commercial Bank and Hatton could not acquire more than 10 percent.

Ranjit Ratnayake, DFCC deputy general manager for planning and development, told Reuters on Wednesday the talks with Standard Chartered were making progress and he was hopeful of an eventual announcement on a deal.
He declined to say when such an announcement might be made.
"We are examining the figures," Ratnayake said. "We are negotiating with Standard Chartered."
Prelis said DFCC was considering taking stakes in other banks too but declined to give details. ($1=58.7 rupees) -- Colombo newsroom (941) 434319
